definitions.change: current minus prior, million kWh; percentage = change / prior x 100

classes.unavailable: a missing observation, or a prior value of zero or less

definitions.contributions: changes of the four sectors and the rounding residual, only when every month involved reconciles within rounding
definitions.monthly_finding: at least one analyzed sector up and another down in the same month; one finding per month
definitions.period: sum each sector over identical complete periods, then compare; growth rates are never averaged

reconciliation.basis: five values each published to 0.001; independent rounding allows 5 x 0.0005
reconciliation.identity: residential + commercial + industrial + transportation = total retail sales

definitions.threshold: 1% is a fixed, transparent product filter: not statistical significance, not empirically calibrated, not proof of materiality.
definitions.values: Retail sales in million kWh as published in the CSV (three decimals), exact decimal arithmetic.

limitations: Residential, commercial and industrial sales include electricity used to operate and move electric vehicles (Table 7.6 footnote b). Electric vehicle use is a separate estimate; it is neither added nor subtracted here.
Transportation covers sales to public railroads and railway systems only (footnote e), not electricity used by road vehicles. It is shown as context and never enters a finding.
Industrial retail sales leave out direct use (self-generated electricity used on site, footnote g), so they are not total industrial electricity use.
The sectors are EIA classes of service (footnotes a to d). The section notes on coverage and the sources were not retained, so billing-period conventions are not established here.
The 1% band is a fixed product filter: not statistical significance, not an empirically calibrated threshold and not proof of materiality.
The comparison scope is fixed. It does not move when newer data appear, and the last month in the retained file is not necessarily the latest month EIA has published since.
The CSV states no edition. The retained PDF prints the September 2026 edition; that edition is not assigned to the CSV, and values agreeing between them would show consistency, not a shared vintage.

scope: Retrospective view of retained EIA data: retail electricity sales to the residential, commercial and industrial sectors, each month compared with the same month a year earlier, from the Monthly Energy Review Table 7.6 kept on this computer. footnotes.a: Electricity sales to ultimate customers based on classes of service reported by electric utilities and, beginning in 1996, other energy service providers.
footnotes.b: Electricity sales to the residential, commercial, and industrial sectors, based on class of service, including sales of electricity to operate and move electric vehicles. See Note 4, "Estimates of Electric Vehicle Use," at end of section.
footnotes.c: Commercial sector, including public street and highway lighting, interdepartmental sales, and other sales to public authorities.
footnotes.d: Industrial sector. Through 2002, excludes agriculture and irrigation; beginning in 2003, includes agriculture and irrigation.
footnotes.e: Sales to public railroads and railway systems only. Excludes the estimated amount of electricity used to operate and move electric vehicles.
footnotes.g: Use of electricity that is 1) self-generated, 2) produced by either the same entity that consumes the power or an affiliate, and 3) used in direct support of a service or industrial process located within the same facility or group of facilities that house the generating equipment. Direct use is exclusive of station use.
footnotes.h: The sum of "Total Sales to Ultimate Customers" and "Direct Use."
footnotes.i: Electricity used to operate and move on-road light-duty electric vehicles (less than or equal to 8,500 pounds). Excludes motor gasoline consumption by plug-in hybrid electric vehicles. Electric vehicle use is estimated independently and should not be added to the sales or total end use columns as it will result in double counting. See Note 4, "Estimates of Electric Vehicle Use," at end of section.
footnotes.j: Beginning in 2023, the estimates are not strictly comparable with earlier years due to a change in the estimation methodology for vehicle miles traveled. For details see Table 1.9 footnote f.
